excluded_families.reason: The effective sample is about 3.2k development rows per asset/task; larger sequence models have an unfavorable parameter-to-sample ratio and are not needed beyond a small GRU.
HistGradientBoosting provides a maintained tree-boosting benchmark without another dependency or materially expanding the bounded model comparison.
The sample and number of temporal folds do not justify a fitted meta learner; an equal-weight ensemble uses only development OOF predictions and has no extra tuning.
Unbounded search would invalidate comparable tuning budgets and encourage selection on validation noise.

fairness: Same rows, folds, transformations, scoring, test period, and three-configuration budget for each tunable family and each primary information set.

configs.rule: future RV = current RV*sqrt(h); future downside = current downside*h; future Amihud = current Amihud
mean log1p target in that training fold
unweighted mean of selected OOF predictions from Ridge, RBF_SVR, ExtraTrees, HistGradientBoosting, MLP, GRU; no fitted meta learner

preprocessing: StandardScaler fitted within each training fold for linear, kernel, MLP and GRU models. Tree models receive training-fold-scaled features too for a uniform pipeline. No imputation, feature selection, or global normalization.
primary_metric: MAE on log1p(target); lower is better. All model/information-set comparisons use the same target rows.
secondary_metrics: MAE and RMSE on original scale
QLIKE on future realized variance (RV target squared)
